question: A team keeps needing to remind Claude Code, in every new session, that all database migrations must be reversible and that API endpoints must follow their internal REST naming convention. What is the most effective way to make Claude apply these rules automatically across sessions in this repository?
options: A) Configure a PostToolUse hook that rejects any file edit violating the naming convention
B) Paste the rules into the first prompt of every new session before asking Claude to make changes
C) Add the rules to a CLAUDE.md file at the repository root so Claude loads them as persistent project context
D) Create a subagent named standards-checker and manually invoke it before every change
correct_answers: C) Add the rules to a CLAUDE.md file at the repository root so Claude loads them as persistent project context
explanations: Incorrect. A hook could enforce the naming convention deterministically, but reversibility of a migration is a semantic judgment a shell command cannot reliably check, and this does not address making Claude aware of the rules as general guidance.
Incorrect. Manually pasting the rules into every new session still requires the team to remember to do it each time, which is the exact repetitive burden the team is trying to eliminate.

Correct. CLAUDE.md is loaded automatically as persistent project memory at the start of every session in that repository, so the team never has to re-paste the rules, directly solving the repeated-reminder problem.

Incorrect. A subagent that must be manually invoked before every change still depends on someone remembering to invoke it, so it does not make the rules apply automatically the way persistent project memory does.
